Let $f(x)={x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-28x+32.$ We know that $(x-4)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ and we need to find its other factors.

Because $(x-4)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ we know that $(x-4)$ divides $f(x)$ with no remainder. So, to begin factoring $f(x),$ we can divide it by $(x-4)$ using synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{4}$ | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-3$ | $-28$ | $32$ |
|  | $↓$ | $4$ | $8$ | $20$ | $-32$ |
|  | $1$ | $2$ | $5$ | $-8$ | $0$ |

Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-28x+32}{x-4}={x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+5x-8,
$$

which means that

$$
{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-28x+32=(x-4)({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+5x-8).
$$

Now, because $(x-1)$ is also a factor of $f(x),$ it must be a factor of the quotient $({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+5x-8).$ So, we divide this quotient by $(x-1)$ using synthetic division once more:

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $5$ | $-8$ |
|  | $↓$ | $1$ | $3$ | $8$ |
|  | $1$ | $3$ | $8$ | $0$ |

Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+5x-8}{x-1}={x}^{2}+3x+8,
$$

which means that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-28x+32 & =(x-4)(x-1)({x}^{2}+3x+8)\end{aligned}
$$

To see whether the quadratic polynomial ${x}^{2}+3x+8$ can be factored any further, we calculate its discriminant:

$$
{b}^{2}-4ac=(3)^{2}-4(1)(8)=-23<0
$$

So, the quadratic polynomial ${x}^{2}+3x+8$ cannot be factored over the real numbers since its discriminant is negative. 

Therefore, the full factorization of $f(x)$ over the real numbers is given by 

$$
{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-28x+32=(x-4)(x-1){{({x}^{2}+3x+8)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}.
$$

Finally, $P(x)={x}^{2}+3x+8.$
